A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same AerialVG work and support comparison of text, equations, figures and tables. Neither contains an appendix or embedded supplement; both mention separate supplementary material that is not supplied.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations in Tables 1–3, and a real-world drone-image grounding example in Figure 6.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original benchmark evaluations, component ablations and real-world drone-image result reported in v1.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same GroundingDINO-based architecture, Hierarchical Cross-Attention, Relation-Aware Grounding, scoring procedure and losses. The two-stage training procedure in Section 5.1 is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use AerialVG, RefCOCO, RefCOCO+ and RefCOCOg, and report the same DJI M30T aerial test scenario. Dataset construction, annotation scope and represented tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 retain the same comparators: TranVG, Dynamic-MDETR, SimVG and Grounding DINO. The additional introductory citations do not introduce evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: The zero-shot and fine-tuning comparisons, Top-1/Top-5 metrics, reported benchmark splits, backbones and training settings are unchanged. Section 5.5 retains drone imagery captured at 50 meters with 4000×3000 resolution.

E4.justification: Table 3 retains the attention-only, relation-only and combined-component ablations. Section 5.5 and Figure 6 retain the same real-world qualitative case, with no added robustness, sensitivity or error analyses.

E5.justification: Neither supplied version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both present the same point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3, dataset-statistics figures and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains AerialVG's fine-tuned Top-1/Top-5 scores of 50.01/87.00 and Grounding DINO's 29.36/78.87; Figure 6 retains the output score of 0.70.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4, attention-update definitions, pairwise relation-matrix construction and loss formulation are unchanged. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same task and first-dataset claims, two architectural contributions, and claims of superior AerialVG performance and competitive RefCOCO results.

C2.justification: Both attribute improved candidate retrieval to Hierarchical Cross-Attention and spatial disambiguation to Relation-Aware Grounding. Section 6 retains the limitation concerning unstructured background information, including roads, and the same future-work direction.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the advertised code location from Ideal-ljl/UAVVG to Ideal-ljl/AerialVG. Both still describe the release as forthcoming; implementation and reproducibility details in Section 5.1 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction adds citations to Fast Rolling Shutter Correction in the Wild and Implicit Event-RGBD Neural SLAM. A published LiveScene entry is also added alongside the already cited preprint of the same work. The related-work discussion and novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The author line reverses the order of Bin Zhao and Xuelong Li and revises superscript markers. Citation callouts and version information are updated, while the body prose and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Additional bibliography entries redistribute references across pages 10–11, accompanied by small front-matter spacing changes. Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–3 retain their content, captions, design and placement.

improvement.justification: The author, citation and prospective code-location updates leave the scientific argument, empirical support, explanations and limitations effectively unchanged. The supplied PDFs establish no meaningful net gain or loss in rigor, clarity or reproducibility.
